statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-47241 (GHSA-c4fp-cxrr-mj66): in the Ruby net-imap gem, the check that stops a raw string argument from ending in a literal marker misses {0} and {0+}, so an attacker-controlled search key, sort or thread key, or fetch attribute ending in {0} makes the server absorb the next command and the connection hangs (a denial of service): https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-c4fp-cxrr-mj66. Upstream fixed it in net-imap 0.4.25 on the 0.4 line, 0.5.15 on the 0.5 line and 0.6.4.1 on the 0.6 line; the 0.4.25 release notes list CVE-2026-47241: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.4.25. The DHI ruby-3.3 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 3.3.10-r0, 3.3.10-r1, 3.3.11-r1, 3.3.11-r2, 3.3.11-r3, 3.3.12-r3, 3.3.13-r3, 3.3.14-r3 and 3.3.14-r4, for x86_64 and aarch64 (ruby-3.3-libs and ruby-3.3-full 3.3.11-r1 are published for aarch64 only). It ships net-imap in its ruby3.3-net-imap gem package, which carries the gem's version rather than Ruby's, so the range below is written in the ruby-3.3 package's own versions, and each ruby-3.3 build is placed by the net-imap its ruby3.3-net-imap package installs. The gem package keeps the gem's own version but takes its -rN release number from the Ruby build that produced it, and the repository keeps one copy of each package version, so the gem package versions published under a given -rN are exactly the net-imap releases the Ruby builds with that -rN shipped. We read Net::IMAP::VERSION in lib/net/imap.rb of every published ruby3.3-net-imap package for both architectures, each verified against the repository index checksum, and listed the contents of every published ruby-3.3-libs package: the published ruby3.3-net-imap packages are 0.4.21-r0, 0.4.21-r1, 0.4.21-r2, 0.4.21-r3, 0.4.25-r3 and 0.4.25-r4. 0.4.21-r0, -r1 and -r2 install net-imap 0.4.21, which Ruby 3.3.10 and 3.3.11 bundle, per https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v3_3_11/gems/bundled_gems, so the -r0, -r1 and -r2 builds, 3.3.10-r0 through 3.3.11-r2, ship 0.4.21. Under -r3 two gem versions exist: 0.4.21-r3, which despite its label installs net-imap 0.4.24 (ruby-3.3-libs 3.3.11-r3 still carries the net-imap-0.4.24 gem archive that install left behind, and no other ruby-3.3-libs build carries a net-imap archive), and 0.4.25-r3, which installs net-imap 0.4.25. Ruby 3.3.11 bundles net-imap 0.4.21 and Ruby 3.3.12 onward bundles 0.4.25, per https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v3_3_12/gems/bundled_gems, so 3.3.11-r3 is the build that replaced its bundled 0.4.21 with 0.4.24, and 3.3.12-r3, 3.3.13-r3 and 3.3.14-r3 ship the bundled 0.4.25. 0.4.25-r4 installs net-imap 0.4.25, so 3.3.14-r4 ships 0.4.25. Both architectures agree for every build. Every ruby-3.3 build before 3.3.12-r3 ships a net-imap without this fix, and 3.3.12-r3 is the first that ships net-imap 0.4.25, so the range is introduced at the first published build and fixed at 3.3.12-r3.

CVE-2026-47241 (GHSA-c4fp-cxrr-mj66): in the Ruby net-imap gem before 0.6.4.1 (and 0.5.15), the check that stops a raw-data argument (criteria for #search and #uid_search, search keys for #sort, #thread, #uid_sort and #uid_thread, attr for #fetch and #uid_fetch) from ending in a literal-continuation marker does not match {0} or {0+}, so input ending that way makes the command absorb the next command and hang until the connection closes, a denial of service: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-c4fp-cxrr-mj66. On the 0.6 release line it is fixed in net-imap 0.6.4.1 by https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/pull/700, commit https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/commit/d6ddd294c588578f6d8dad588716c62f424af2f7, which widens the trailing-marker pattern in RawData#validate in lib/net/imap/command_data.rb to also reject {0} and {0+}; the 0.6.4.1 release notes list this advisory: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.6.4.1. The DHI ruby-4.0 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 4.0.1-r0, 4.0.1-r1, 4.0.2-r1, 4.0.2-r2, 4.0.3-r2, 4.0.4-r2, 4.0.4-r3, 4.0.5-r3, 4.0.6-r3, 4.0.6-r4, 4.0.7-r4, 4.0.9-r4, 4.0.10-r4 and 4.0.10-r5, for x86_64 and aarch64. Ruby bundles net-imap as a gem, which this source ships in its ruby4.0-net-imap package; that package carries the gem's version rather than Ruby's, so the range below is written in the ruby-4.0 package's own versions and each ruby-4.0 build is placed by the net-imap it ships. We downloaded every package built from the ruby-4.0 source in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository as published on 2026-11-28, 654 package files across both architectures, checked each against its repository index checksum and listed every file in them. net-imap is installed only by ruby4.0-net-imap; the only other net-imap file is a cached net-imap-0.6.4.gem archive in ruby-4.0-libs 4.0.4-r3 and 4.0.5-r3, which Ruby does not load. The published ruby4.0-net-imap packages, by Net::IMAP::VERSION in their lib/net/imap.rb: 0.6.2-r0, 0.6.2-r1 and 0.6.2-r2 install net-imap 0.6.2; 0.6.2-r3, despite its label, installs net-imap 0.6.4; 0.6.4.1-r3, 0.6.4.1-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5 install net-imap 0.6.4.1. Their lib/net/imap/command_data.rb matches that file in the corresponding upstream release byte for byte; only the 0.6.4.1 copy has the widened pattern, while 0.6.2 has no trailing-marker check and 0.6.4 has the check that misses {0}. In the repository index each published ruby4.0-net-imap package has the same build time as the ruby-4.0 build that produced it: 0.6.2-r0 with 4.0.1-r0, 0.6.2-r1 with 4.0.2-r1, 0.6.2-r2 with 4.0.4-r2, 0.6.2-r3 with 4.0.5-r3, 0.6.4.1-r3 with 4.0.6-r3, 0.6.4.1-r4 with 4.0.10-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5 with 4.0.10-r5. The other ruby-4.0 builds produced a gem package version that was already published, so they are placed by the Ruby release: Ruby 4.0.1 to 4.0.5 bundle net-imap 0.6.2 and Ruby 4.0.6 and later bundle 0.6.4.1 (gems/bundled_gems at the v4.0.1 to v4.0.10 tags), and ruby-4.0-libs 4.0.4-r3 carries the net-imap 0.6.4 gem archive left by the step that replaced its bundled net-imap. So every ruby-4.0 build before 4.0.6-r3 ships net-imap 0.6.2 or 0.6.4, both affected, and 4.0.6-r3 and every later build ship net-imap 0.6.4.1. Both architectures agree for every build. The range is introduced at the first published build and fixed at 4.0.6-r3.

We downloaded every package built from the ruby-4.0 source in the DHI Alpine 3.24 repository as published on 2026-11-28, 326 package files across both architectures, checked each against its repository index checksum and listed every file in them. net-imap is installed only by ruby4.0-net-imap; the only other net-imap file is a cached net-imap-0.6.4.gem archive in ruby-4.0-libs 4.0.5-r3, which Ruby does not load. The published ruby4.0-net-imap packages, by Net::IMAP::VERSION in their lib/net/imap.rb: 0.6.2-r3, despite its label, installs net-imap 0.6.4; 0.6.4.1-r3, 0.6.4.1-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5 install net-imap 0.6.4.1. Their lib/net/imap/command_data.rb matches that file in the corresponding upstream release byte for byte; only the 0.6.4.1 copy has the widened pattern, while 0.6.2 has no trailing-marker check and 0.6.4 has the check that misses {0}. In the repository index each published ruby4.0-net-imap package has the same build time as the ruby-4.0 build that produced it: 0.6.2-r3 with 4.0.5-r3, 0.6.4.1-r3 with 4.0.6-r3, 0.6.4.1-r4 with 4.0.10-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5 with 4.0.10-r5. 4.0.6-r4, 4.0.7-r4 and 4.0.9-r4 produced a gem package version that was already published; Ruby 4.0.6 and later bundle net-imap 0.6.4.1 (gems/bundled_gems at the v4.0.6 to v4.0.10 tags). So 4.0.5-r3, the first build in this repository, ships net-imap 0.6.4, which is affected, and 4.0.6-r3 and every later build ship net-imap 0.6.4.1. Both architectures agree for every build. The range is introduced at the first published build and fixed at 4.0.6-r3.
